title: GTM Engineering: The Technical Bits — Everett Berry, Clay
talk_summary: A GTM-engineering talk about building data layers, orchestration graphs, and long-running per-account agents for sales/marketing automation at Clay.

takeaways.evidence_quote: an agent that exists for each account and maintains a persistent state of that account... it's often going to be dormant... use smart triggers or a heartbeat or something to wake it up

takeaways.technique: Separate agent-written fields from deterministic/human fields
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the fields agents update distinct from fields written by deterministic systems or humans, so automated reasoning never clobbers authoritative data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I always recommend separating the fields that agents are updating from the fields that deterministic systems are updating or that people are updating

takeaways.technique: Graph of general-purpose nodes (agent, tool-call, conditional, code, map-reduce)
takeaways.what_they_do: Model orchestration as a graph of a few reusable node types — agent, tool call, conditional, code, and map-reduce fan-out/fan-in — instead of bespoke per-workflow logic.

takeaways.technique: Explicit waits/loops for eventually-consistent external systems
takeaways.what_they_do: When two external systems sync independently, insert waits and polling loops to confirm data is ready before acting on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you actually need to introduce things like weights and loops to check if information is ready

takeaways.technique: Waterfall across providers with evals to pick the best source
takeaways.what_they_do: Query multiple data providers and run evals to measure which provider is most accurate per field, then layer them to maximize coverage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: either you or the vendor that you're using needs to run evals against these data providers in order to obtain the most accurate information
takeaways.numbers: Forager alone got 'only halfway' on phone numbers
